reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) concerns thermal stability and grain growth in different HEA systems (refractory HEA films and a CoCrFeMnNi-type alloy), not alumina coatings, oxidation resistance, or the HfNbTaTiZr alloy. None of the key premises about coating deposition, adhesion, oxygen barrier effectiveness, or mechanical property retention are supported by the provided passages.
premises: A CVD alumina coating can be deposited on HfNbTaTiZr at ~1000 °C to form a dense, adherent oxygen barrier.
The alumina coating will remain stable and adherent during 100 h at 1000 °C in air.
The coating will prevent oxygen ingress and preserve the underlying cast microstructure.
The coated alloy will retain similar yield strength and ductility to the untreated cast alloy at room temperature and 1000 °C.
